title: Microsoft Dataverse: unlicensed Entra users as activity recipients

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: The admin path, required roles, recipient licence exemption and roadmap details are supported. However, the documentation does not establish that the feature is portal-only or included in a named existing licence; those assertions should be narrowed to what Microsoft documents.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is in-development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: General availability is targeted for January CY2027.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "January CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap gives October CY2026 as the preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Microsoft 365 app, Dynamics 365 Sales, Dynamics 365 Customer Service and Microsoft Dataverse.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft 365 app", "Dynamics 365 Sales", "Dynamics 365 Customer Service", "Microsoft Dataverse"]

claims.claim: The feature is admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: By default, you can only add users with a Dataverse or Power Apps license to activities in Dynamics 365 apps. Turn on the *Activities for users without licenses* feature in the Power Platform admin center

claims.claim: The feature's licensing model is included in an existing product licence.
claims.quote: Searched: "Add users without licenses" activities pricing charge license; "add-unlicensed-users-activities" "license" pricing included. Read feature page; it exempts recipients but names no licence that includes the feature.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to unknown unless a Microsoft source explicitly establishes inclusion in a named existing licence. Retain the supported notes that recipients need no Dataverse or Power Apps licence and cannot run Dynamics 365 apps; distinguish that exemption from the feature's overall licensing.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Recipients do not need a Dataverse or Power Apps licence to be added to activity recipient fields.
claims.quote: Turn on this feature in the Power Platform admin center to allow users with a Microsoft Entra ID to be added to activity recipient fields without requiring a Dataverse or Power Apps license.

claims.claim: The feature allows active Microsoft Entra users in the tenant to be activity recipients in Dynamics 365 apps.
claims.quote: Users without licenses are people in your tenant who have an active Microsoft Entra ID account but don't have a Dataverse or Power Apps license.
claims.fix: Introduce the behavior as 'Activities for users without licenses is currently documented as a preview feature; the following behavior and licensing describe that preview.' The cited feature page is titled 'Add users without licenses to activity recipient fields (preview)'.

claims.claim: Supported email recipient fields include To, Cc and Bcc.
claims.quote: such as the To, Cc, or Bcc fields of an email

claims.claim: The feature supports appointment attendees.
claims.quote: Required Attendees, Optional attendees of appointment

claims.claim: The feature supports Call From and Call To fields on phone calls.
claims.quote: Call From, or Call To of phone call.

claims.claim: Without enabling this feature, the default restriction is that only users with a Dataverse or Power Apps licence can be added to Dynamics 365 activities.
claims.quote: By default, you can only add users with a Dataverse or Power Apps license to activities in Dynamics 365 apps.

claims.claim: After the feature is enabled, the user lookup uses the Microsoft Entra ID table.
claims.quote: After you enable the *Activities for users without licenses* feature in the Power Platform admin center, the user lookup uses the **Microsoft Entra ID** table

claims.claim: The Microsoft Entra ID table is a virtual Dataverse table displaying active Entra users.
claims.quote: a virtual Dataverse table that displays the current list of active Microsoft Entra ID users.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Selecting a Microsoft Entra user for an activity creates a corresponding unlicensed-user record in the environment.
claims.quote: When you select a Microsoft Entra ID user for an activity, Dataverse creates a corresponding unlicensed-user record in the environment so that the user can be added to the activity's recipient fields.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The newly created unlicensed-user record has disabled status.
claims.quote: The user record is created with a disabled status.

claims.where: licensing.notes; What's changing; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: These unlicensed recipients cannot sign in to or run Dynamics 365 apps.
claims.quote: These users can be included as recipients, but they can't sign in to or run Dynamics 365 apps.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Assigning a licence automatically updates the unlicensed user to a licensed user.
claims.quote: When a user without a license is assigned a license, the user is automatically updated to a licensed user and can use the application based on their assigned security roles and permissions.

claims.claim: Earlier activities remain associated with the same user record after licence assignment.
claims.quote: Activities previously associated with the user remain associated with the same user record. No migration or conversion of the user or their existing activities is required.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: All users in the tenant must receive read permission on the Microsoft Entra ID table before the feature is enabled.
claims.quote: Before you turn on the feature in the Power Platform admin center, you need to grant all users in the tenant **read** permission on the **Microsoft Entra ID** table.

claims.claim: Existing security roles can be updated to grant read access to the Microsoft Entra ID table.
claims.quote: Update each existing security role assigned to users and add **read** permission for the **Microsoft Entra ID** table.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; At rollout
claims.claim: A custom role granting read permission on the Microsoft Entra ID table can instead be assigned to all users.
claims.quote: Create a custom security role that grants **read** permission for the **Microsoft Entra ID** table, and then assign the role to all users.

claims.claim: Privileged Role Administrator is required for the step granting table read access.
claims.quote: You need to be a **Privileged Role Administrator** in the Microsoft Entra admin center to grant users read access to the Microsoft Entra ID table.

claims.claim: Power Platform administrator is required to enable the feature.
claims.quote: You need to be a **Power Platform administrator** to turn on the feature in Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: The switch is in Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Activities for users without licenses > Add anyone with an Entra ID to an activity's recipients fields.
claims.quote:
Select **Settings**.
5. Select **Product**, and then select **Features**.
6. Go to **Activities for users without licenses**.
7. Select the **Add anyone with an Entra ID to an activity's recipients fields** checkbox.

claims.claim: The documented switch is configured per environment.
claims.quote: In the **Manage** pane, select **Environments**. Then select an environment.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API or automation equivalent for this feature's switch.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse unlicensed users activity recipients organization table API setting EnableUnlicensed. Opened feature page and pac env; searched Organization reference for unlicen, recipient, aaduser, entra. No feature switch identified.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a tenant-wide default control for this feature on either the admin UI or API surface.
claims.quote: Searched: "Activities for users without licenses" "tenant-wide"; Dataverse "activity" "unlicensed" "tenant" settings default. Read feature page and Tenant settings. No tenant-wide default control found.

claims.claim: pac env update-settings is documented for changing environment organization settings generally.
claims.quote: The pac env list-settings command returns all the columns from the first and only row of the [organization entity type](/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/reference/organization). Use `pac env update-settings` to change those settings.

claims.claim: The feature's switch is portal-only.
claims.quote: Searched: "Activities for users without licenses" API organization setting tenant default PowerShell. Read feature and pac env pages; searched Organization reference. None states that only the portal can set it.
claims.fix: Replace 'The switch is per environment and portal-only' with 'The switch is per environment. As of November 2026, Microsoft documents the admin UI but no feature-specific API or automation equivalent.' Keep controls[0].api null; absence of API documentation does not establish a portal-only restriction.

claims.claim: No feature-specific charge is published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Add users without licenses" activities pricing charge license; "add-unlicensed-users-activities" "license" pricing included. Read the feature page and licensing search results; none publishes a charge for this recipient feature.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The documented setup requires administrator effort to grant read access and enable the setting, supporting a low known implementation cost.
claims.quote: Before you turn on the feature in the Power Platform admin center, you need to grant all users in the tenant **read** permission on the **Microsoft Entra ID** table.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters
claims.claim: The Microsoft Entra ID lookup exposes basic directory information about users.
claims.quote:
| Description | **The name displayed in the address book for the user.** |
| DisplayName | **Display Name** |
| IsValidForForm | True |
| IsValidForRead | True |
claims.fix: Add the Microsoft Entra ID (aaduser) table reference to sources to substantiate the directory-attributes exposure: https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/reference/entities/aaduser.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist instructs administrators to configure Entra ID table read permission, but that control has no row in the controls table.
claims.quote: Plan the security role change: update existing roles or create a custom role with read on the Entra ID table. | Controls: Whether unlicensed Entra users can be activity recipients; Tenant-wide default for the feature.
claims.fix: Add a controls row for 'Who can read the Microsoft Entra ID table', covering the security-role prerequisite and linking to https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/add-unlicensed-users-activities#grant-users-read-access-to-the-microsoft-entra-id-table. Research its UI and API surfaces before filling them.
